title: Integration test output must report goal-proximity metric as a pass/fail gate for candidate branches
description: The current integration test output surfaces rubric pass/fail for the specific change under test. It does not answer 'does this bring us closer to the north star?' A goal-proximity metric — computed as criteria satisfied post-implementation vs pre-implementation — makes every candidate branch self-evidencing: a candidate that passes all rubrics but leaves goal proximity unchanged has addressed the wrong thing; a candidate that increases proximity while passing rubrics has demonstrably advanced the project. Without this gate, QA can pass for an implementation that is technically correct but strategically wrong.
proposed_resolution: 1. Extend the integration test harness to compute goal proximity before and after applying the candidate branch: read `.moeb/goal.md`, evaluate each criterion against the signal catalogue state (pre: without this branch's resolved signals; post: with this branch's resolved signals). 2. Express the metric as `N/M criteria satisfied (X%)` with a delta indicator (`+N`, `0`, `-N` relative to pre-branch baseline). Emit as a `goal_proximity` block in the run artefact JSON: `{ pre: { satisfied: N, total: M }, post: { satisfied: N, total: M }, delta: N }`. 3. The candidate gate enforces `goal_proximity.delta >= 0` — a regressing candidate fails even if all rubrics pass. A flat delta (0) is a warning, not a hard failure, unless the signal's `proposed_resolution` explicitly claims goal-criterion advancement. 4. Display a per-criterion breakdown in the test output so the run agent can diagnose which criterion failed to advance and produce a targeted follow-up signal.
